questions.question: A statement is followed by two courses of action, numbered I and II. You must assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the following course(s) of action logically follow(s) for pursuing. Statement: The local park has become littered with trash, making it unpleasant for visitors. Courses of action: I) The city council should place more trash bins around the park. II) The city council should close the park until it is cleaned.
questions.questionHtml:
A statement is followed by two courses of action, numbered I and II. You must assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the following course(s) of action logically follow(s) for pursuing.
Statement: The local park has become littered with trash, making it unpleasant for visitors.
Courses of action:
I) The city council should place more trash bins around the park.

II) The city council should close the park until it is cleaned.
questions.solution:
Given the statement: The local park has become littered with trash, making it unpleasant for visitors.

Let's analyze the courses of action:

Course of Action I: Placing more trash bins is a logical step to encourage proper disposal of litter and maintain cleanliness in the park.

Course of Action II: Closing the park might be an extreme measure and not necessarily solve the problem of littering. Educating visitors and providing facilities to manage waste are more constructive approaches.

Thus, only Course of Action I follows logically.

questions.question: Read the given statement and inferences carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given inferences can be derived from the statement. (An inference is something which is not directly stated but can be derived from the given facts/information in the statement.) Statement: All birds have feathers. Inferences: I. Penguins have feathers. II. All creatures with feathers are birds.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statement and inferences carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given inferences can be derived from the statement.
(An inference is something which is not directly stated but can be derived from the given facts/information in the statement.)
Statement: All birds have feathers.
Inferences:
I. Penguins have feathers.

II. All creatures with feathers are birds.
questions.solution:
Statement: All birds have feathers.

Inferences:

Inference I: Since penguins are birds, and the statement says all birds have feathers, it follows that penguins have feathers. Thus, Inference I is correct.

Inference II: The statement only confirms that all birds have feathers but does not imply that only birds can have feathers. There may be other animals or creatures (hypothetically) that could have feathers. Hence, Inference II is incorrect.
